html:
1What You Will Learn

Note

Acronyms in this note. CI/CD: continuous integration and continuous delivery; PR: pull request; JSON: JavaScript Object Notation; MCP: Model Context Protocol

  • Plan mode versus direct execution, and the Explore subagent
  • Four iterative refinement techniques: examples, test-driven iteration, the interview pattern, one message versus many
  • Running Claude Code in CI/CD: -p, --output-format json, --json-schema, CLAUDE.md for context, independent review, no duplicate comments

2Plan Mode or Direct Execution (Task 3.4)

Running case

Two Tickets at Birchwood Supply

  • Ticket A: "The checkout page crashes with a stack trace pointing to formatPrice when the price is null"
  • Ticket B: "Replace the charting library in the reporting module; it touches more than 40 files, and two candidate libraries need different hosting setups"

Plan mode lets Claude explore the code and design an approach without making changes. You review the plan, then approve it for execution.

Plan mode Direct execution
Choose it for Complex tasks: large-scale changes, several valid approaches, architectural decisions, multi-file modifications (microservice restructuring, a library migration touching 45+ files, choosing between integration approaches with different infrastructure needs) Simple, well-scoped changes: a single-file bug fix with a clear stack trace, adding one validation check
Benefit Safe exploration and design before committing; avoids costly rework Fast, no overhead
Wrong choice costs Overhead for trivial work Late discovery of dependencies and rework

  • Combine them: plan mode to investigate and plan (for example a library migration), then direct execution to carry out the chosen plan.
  • Explore subagent: a built-in subagent that does verbose discovery work in its own context and returns a summary, so the main conversation does not fill up during multi-phase tasks.
  • If the complexity is already stated in the requirements (dozens of files, boundary decisions), start in plan mode; do not "see if it gets complicated".

[Verify live] Enter plan mode with Shift+Tab or claude --permission-mode plan; Claude reads and proposes a plan but makes no edits until you approve. Explore and Plan are built-in, read-only subagents. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

Complexity that is already stated in the requirements (dozens of files, several approaches) means plan mode now, not "switch if it gets hard".

3Iterative Refinement (Task 3.5)

Technique Use it when How
Concrete input/output examples Prose descriptions are interpreted inconsistently Give 2 to 3 examples of the input and the exact expected output
Test-driven iteration You can specify behavior as tests Write the test suite first (expected behavior, edge cases, performance), then iterate by sharing test failures
Interview pattern The domain is unfamiliar or has hidden design choices Have Claude ask you questions first (cache invalidation? failure modes?) before implementing
Specific test cases An edge case is mishandled (null values in a migration) Provide the case with example input and expected output
One message vs several Problems interact Put all interacting issues in one detailed message; fix independent problems one at a time

Exam tip

Output formats keep coming back different from what you described? → show 2 to 3 concrete before/after examples, not a longer prose description.

4Claude Code in CI/CD (Task 3.6)

Need Use
Run without interactive input (a plain claude "..." hangs waiting) -p (or --print): process the prompt, print the result, exit
Machine-readable results --output-format json and --json-schema (structured findings to post as inline PR comments)
Project context for CI runs CLAUDE.md: testing standards, fixture conventions, review criteria
Avoid duplicate comments after new commits Include prior review findings in the context and tell Claude to report only new or still-unaddressed issues
Avoid duplicate test suggestions Provide the existing test files in context
Better test generation Document testing standards, what makes a valuable test, and available fixtures in CLAUDE.md 
claude -p "Review this pull request for security issues" \
  --output-format json \
  --json-schema '{"type":"object","properties":{"findings":{"type":"array","items":{"type":"object","properties":{"file":{"type":"string"},"line":{"type":"integer"},"severity":{"type":"string"},"issue":{"type":"string"}},"required":["file","issue"]}}},"required":["findings"]}'
  • Independent review instance: the session that generated the code retains its reasoning, so it is less likely to question its own work. Use a second, independent Claude Code instance (no generator reasoning) to review.
  • Distractors: there is no CLAUDE_HEADLESS environment variable and no --batch flag for this purpose; redirecting stdin from /dev/null does not make Claude Code non-interactive.

[Verify live] The structured result appears in the JSON output's structured_output field (check it exists before using it). --bare starts faster and is recommended for scripted calls, but it skips auto-discovery of CLAUDE.md, hooks, skills and MCP servers: if you use it, pass context explicitly (for example --append-system-prompt or --mcp-config). Add --allowedTools or a permission mode so no step waits for approval. As of 8 November 2026.

Exam tip

In CI always use -p; for machine-readable output add --output-format json with --json-schema; give context through CLAUDE.md.

5Exam Q&A

S1Birchwood must replace the charting library in its reporting module. More than 40 files are affected, and the two candidate libraries need different hosting setups. Which approach is best?

  • AWrite exhaustive upfront instructions and execute directly
  • BPick a library at random and start editing
  • CStart directly and switch to plan mode only if unexpected problems appear later
  • DEnter plan mode to explore usage, compare the options and design the migration before changing code
Show the answer

Answer: D. A multi-file change with several valid approaches and infrastructure consequences is what plan mode is for. Waiting for trouble ignores that the complexity is already known.

S2A stack trace shows formatPrice crashing on a null price in one file. What is the best mode?

  • ACreate a new service
  • BDirect execution with a null check
  • CPlan mode with a full architecture review
  • DAsk for a plan document first
Show the answer

Answer: B. A clear, single-file fix is well scoped; direct execution is efficient.

S3During a multi-phase migration, discovery output (hundreds of lines of file listings) fills the main context. What helps most?

  • ATurn off exploration
  • BUse the Explore subagent so that verbose discovery stays out of the main context
  • CIncrease the prompt length limit
  • DPaste the contents of every file into the prompt so that the model never has to explore
Show the answer

Answer: B. The Explore subagent isolates verbose discovery in its own context and returns only a summary.

S4A team describes a conversion rule in prose three times and Claude interprets it differently each time. What works best?

  • ASwitch to a different model
  • BRemove the rule and describe the transformation again in other words
  • CWrite an even longer prose description with more detail and more adjectives
  • DProvide 2 to 3 concrete input/output examples
Show the answer

Answer: D. Concrete input and output examples communicate the expected transformation unambiguously.

S5A developer needs a caching layer in an unfamiliar domain and does not know what could go wrong. Which technique brings up the unknowns?

  • AAsk for the shortest possible solution and add the missing safeguards afterwards
  • BCopy a solution from another project
  • CThe interview pattern: have Claude ask you questions before it implements
  • DImplement immediately
Show the answer

Answer: C. Interviewing first surfaces considerations the developer had not thought of.

S6Three bugs in a pricing function interact (fixing one changes the others). How should they be reported?

  • AAll together in one detailed message
  • BIn separate sessions
  • COne at a time over many messages
  • DOnly the first one, and ignore the rest until the first is completely fixed
Show the answer

Answer: A. Interacting problems should be addressed together; independent problems can be handled sequentially.

S7A nightly job runs claude "Summarize today's failed tests" and never finishes because Claude Code waits for input. What is the correct change?

  • AIncrease the job timeout to several hours so that the run can complete
  • BWrap it in a terminal multiplexer session
  • CRun it with the -p flag so it prints the result and exits
  • DPipe the word yes into the command
Show the answer

Answer: C. -p / --print is the documented non-interactive mode for scripts and CI. Feeding fake input, hiding the terminal or waiting longer does not make the tool non-interactive.

S8A CI job should post findings as inline comments through a script. What should the command output?

  • AA screenshot
  • BFree-form prose that a script splits into comments with regular expressions
  • CAn email
  • DJSON that conforms to a schema (--output-format json, --json-schema)
Show the answer

Answer: D. Machine-parseable structured findings that follow a schema are easy for a script to post as comments.

S9After a developer pushes new commits, the review bot repeats comments already made. How can it avoid duplicates?

  • ALower the model temperature
  • BReview only the first commit
  • CDelete every earlier comment from the pull request before each new review run is started
  • DInclude the earlier findings and tell Claude to report only new or unaddressed issues
Show the answer

Answer: D. Prior findings in the context let Claude suppress what is already reported and mention only new items.

S10Generated tests keep suggesting scenarios that already exist. Which change helps?

  • AUse a shorter prompt
  • BProvide the existing test files in the context
  • CAsk for more tests so that the duplicates are outnumbered
  • DRemove CLAUDE.md so that no standards are loaded into the context
Show the answer

Answer: B. Showing the existing tests lets Claude avoid suggesting scenarios that are already covered.

S11The same Claude Code session that wrote a change is asked to review it and finds nothing. What is the better design?

  • AUse an independent Claude Code instance with no generator reasoning to review
  • BAsk the same session to try harder and turn on extended thinking for the review pass
  • CSkip review
  • DReview only formatting
Show the answer

Answer: A. The generating session keeps its reasoning and is less likely to challenge itself; independent review catches more.

S12Which TWO options help run Claude Code in a pipeline and return machine-parseable findings? Select TWO.

  • A--output-format json together with --json-schema
  • BA --batch flag
  • CAn --interactive flag
  • DThe -p flag
  • EA CLAUDE_HEADLESS environment variable
Show the answer

Answer: A, D. -p prevents waiting for input, and the JSON options give structured output. The other options are not the documented mechanism.

S13Which TWO tasks favor plan mode? Select TWO.

  • ARenaming one local variable
  • BChoosing between two integrations with different infrastructure needs
  • CFixing a typo in a comment
  • DAdding one null check at a stack-trace line
  • EA library migration touching more than 40 files
Show the answer

Answer: B, E. Large multi-file changes and architectural choices benefit from planning before editing. Tiny, well-scoped edits are quicker with direct execution.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Plan mode Complex, multi-file, architectural, several valid approaches; explore and design before changing code
Direct execution Simple, well-scoped (one-file fix with a stack trace)
Both Plan to investigate, then execute directly
Explore subagent Verbose discovery in its own context; returns a summary
Refinement 2 to 3 examples · tests first · interview first · specific edge cases · interacting issues together, independent ones in turn
CI flags -p/--print (no hang) · --output-format json · --json-schema
CI context CLAUDE.md (standards, fixtures, criteria); give prior findings and existing tests
Review Use an independent instance; the generating session reviews itself poorly
Not real CLAUDE_HEADLESS, --batch
